node_labels.a1: The NB, NR and bulk EXAFS transforms superpose in peak position, so no Cu-O or Cu-La bond lengthening is resolved in the figure

node_labels.n19: The nanobamboos are single-phase orthorhombic La2CuO4
node_labels.o4: The observed PXRD pattern coincides with the Rietveld-calculated pattern; the difference curve is flat and no reflection is left unindexed

node_labels.o1: Rugged-surfaced nanofibers about 100-200 nm across interlace into a continuous 3D network

node_labels.o2: One fiber is a chain of roughly 100 nm wide segments joined at narrow necks spaced about 150 nm apart

node_labels.o7: For the NBs at -1.0 V the C2H4 segment spans about 42 to 100% of the stacked FE bar, i.e. FE(C2H4) is about 60%, with H2 about 36%

node_labels.o8: At -1.0 V FE(C2H4) ranks NBs 60% > NRs 12% > bulk 0%, while FE(CO) ranks bulk 91% > NRs 11% > NBs 4%

node_labels.o10: For bulk La2CuO4 the C2H4 contribution is zero at every potential from -0.8 to -1.3 V; only CO, CH4 and H2 appear

node_labels.o9: Over 12 h the NB current density drifts from -2.8 to -4.0 mA/cm2 and the bulk holds near -6.3, while FE points stay at 55-62% C2H4 and about 85% CO

node_labels.o13: The Cu L-edge spectra of all three La2CuO4 samples reproduce the CuO reference peak near 931 eV and lack the Cu2O and Cu-foil features

node_labels.o15: The NB Cu K-edge XANES before reaction, at -1.0 V vs RHE and after reaction share the same edge position and post-edge shape

node_labels.a2: CO2 desorbs at 418 C from the NBs and 408 C from the NRs, and bulk adds a broad peak near 580 C, so CO2 binding ranks bulk > NBs > NRs, opposite to C2H4 selectivity

o12.F6b.why: CORRECT: the candidate reports the same peak temperatures (410 °C NBs, 407 °C NRs, 401 °C bulk) matching the answer key, though it interprets the process as reduction/desorption generically rather than specifically CO desorption.

a3.F6b.why: PARTIAL: The candidate correctly identifies the same underlying data — three TPD-type curves (labeled NBs, NRs, bulk) with peak maxima at 410, 407, and 401 °C (a 9 °C span), matching the key's stated peak spread, and describes the peaks as broad/asymmetric. Instead, the candidate frames the small shift as a meaningful morphology-dependent trend (nanostructured forms requiring slightly higher desorption temperatures), which is a different interpretive emphasis than the key's point about measurement resolution, though it does not contradict the underlying facts (same peaks, same magnitude of shift).
